text:
customer_acme: Hey team — after we uploaded the new cert bundle to our Private VPC load balancer this morning, some clients get intermittent TLS handshake failures and others see 502s. Started ~09:10 UTC. Any quick checks we should run?

emma-support: Sorry you're hitting this. Is this the private/VPC deployment? Can you paste a curl -v or openssl s_client output? Also are you on a strict egress allowlist?

customer_acme: It's Private (VPC). We do have strict egress rules. Here's a sample curl output from a failing client:

```
$ curl -v https://api.acme.internal/health
* Connected to api.acme.internal (10.0.12.5) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 connection using TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* server certificate verification failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (possibly missing intermediate)
* Closing connection 0
curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate
```

emma-support: thx. Can you run this from inside your VPC (to hit same egress path) and paste output?

customer_acme: ran from an app instance:

```
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.0.12.5:443 -servername api.acme.internal -status
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 O = Example CA, CN = Example Root CA
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.acme.internal
   i:/CN=Example Intermediate CA
 1 s:/CN=Example Intermediate CA
   i:/CN=Example Root CA
---
OCSP response: no response sent
---
SSL handshake has read 3271 bytes and written 450 bytes
---
```

luis-sre: OCSP response: no response sent -> that suggests stapling wasn't available. If clients are doing online checks or require stapling (must-staple), this can fail. Two common causes: the LB can't reach CA's OCSP responder due to egress allowlist, or the cert bundle uploaded missed the intermediate.

raj-oncall: Quick repro checklist: (1) confirm intermediate present in bundle (2) check LB if it attempted OCSP fetch during reload (3) verify outbound connectivity from LB/NAT to OCSP responder (port 80/443 depending).

emma-support: Can you show the exact cert bundle you uploaded (PEM) or confirm it includes the intermediate? Also can you paste a tcpdump | grep to the OCSP host from the NAT/gw?

customer_acme: We confirmed bundle includes intermediate (I pasted the PEM to the ticket). I ran a tcpdump on the NAT host and saw SYNs to ocsp.example-ca.com but no replies, RST from our FW: 

```
10:12:34.123456 IP 10.0.1.5.45555 > ocsp.example-ca.com.http: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 64240
10:12:34.123457 IP fw.gw 10.0.1.1 > 10.0.1.5.45555: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0
```

customer_acme: Looks like the firewall was dropping/closing outbound connections to the OCSP host. We recently tightened egress rules earlier today.

luis-sre: That matches. When the LB can't fetch OCSP to staple, OpenSSL shows "no response sent" and some clients that enforce OCSP will fail. Also some client SDKs will treat missing stapled OCSP as cert validation failure.

emma-support: Action plan: 1) temporarily allow outbound to the CA's OCSP responder (port 80/443) from the NAT/gw and LB, 2) reload the cert on LB or trigger a stapling refresh, 3) verify with openssl s_client -status that OCSP Response: good.

infra-bot: Ticket #INC-2026 created (support->infra) and assigned to raj-oncall.

raj-oncall: I've added an allow rule to the egress ACL for ocsp.example-ca.com (and the CA IPs) and asked security to approve permanent exception. Also triggered a config reload on the LB.

customer_acme: After allowlist change + reload:

```
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.0.12.5:443 -servername api.acme.internal -status
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 O = Example CA, CN = Example Root CA
verify return:1
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.acme.internal
   i:/CN=Example Intermediate CA
 1 s:/CN=Example Intermediate CA
   i:/CN=Example Root CA
---
OCSP Response: good
---
SSL handshake has read 4392 bytes and written 450 bytes
---
```

customer_acme: Errors gone, clients are back to healthy. Thanks.

emma-support: Great — root cause = egress allowlist blocked OCSP fetch during rotation which left LB without stapled OCSP responses. Follow-ups: - security to add permanent allowlist to CA OCSP ranges - add a pre-rotation egress check in our runbook so future rotations validate OCSP reachability automatically.

luis-sre: Also added a small health-check in the rotation job that runs `openssl s_client -status` against the new cert before flipping traffic. Saved in INC-2026 notes.

customer_acme: Thanks all :rocket:

emma-support: marking thread resolved, will keep INC-2026 open for the security exception and runbook change. :white_check_mark:
